title: fix(ios): tool steps show outcome unknown instead of their local titles
body: Related: #163543 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: expanded native chat steps show a generic “Exec — outcome unknown” title instead of the tool's local title when the Gateway has no terminal status for the call. ## User Impact User impact: those steps use the native tool title, with the existing command/detail line. This does not turn an unknown outcome into success: unknown outcomes visibly retain “No result” on iPhone as well as in accessibility and on desktop. The shared row is used by both iOS and macOS. ## Why This Change Was Made The Gateway deliberately substitutes an outcome-unknown title for ended calls without a status. Native chat already has a tool display registry; it now uses that local title in this one case and retains Gateway titles for other activity states. The linked issue is broader outcome-projection context, not a claim that this PR fixes missing outcome facts. Fold labels, step counts, and the working line are unchanged. ## Evidence ### Repaired candidate — native validation passed Validated revision: `cab65a8cb82eb9ecca9a6dd46fb1d8e58a1bfcfd`. Colin supplied the Mac-agent report and the two screenshots below on October 8. The report binds both positive runs to this exact published SHA with no tracked changes; RoboClaw independently inspected the supplied images. This is **synthetic local-fixture iPhone simulator proof**, not a physical-device or live Gateway/provider round trip. - **Environment:** Apple silicon; macOS 27.0 (26A5421a), Xcode 27.0 (27A5209h), Swift 6.4; task-owned iPhone 17 Pro simulator, iOS 27.0 (24A5370g). - **Shared activity tests:** 10 executed, all passed. Raw output does not turn an authoritative unknown outcome into success. - **Native build-for-testing:** passed, including embedded Watch targets. Strict iOS SwiftLint: zero violations across 477 files. SwiftFormat lint: 0/477 files require formatting. - **Rendered regression:** one test passed initially, the one-test negative control failed at the intended pixel assertion, then the unchanged candidate passed again. The negative control changes only the mobile outcome-label condition back to desktop-only; it preserves the repaired fixture and test. Failure: “Visible unknown-outcome cue is wrong for printf ready: exec printf ready.” Accessibility had passed, proving this detects the visual regression rather than merely accessibility state. - **Observed pixels:** local Exec titles; visible No result for both unknown cases (with raw output and without output); no such warning for the known-success control. Completed-work expansion and the final reply remain intact. The output-free row need not expand. - **Cleanup reported:** candidate and negative-control worktrees removed, task simulator deleted, temporary tools/DerivedData removed; existing operator app/Gateway/device state preserved. | Before — behavioral negative control | After — exact repaired candidate | |---|---| | ![Negative control: both unknown tool rows lack a visible outcome cue](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0d182f85-69d4-49e5-a9ed-a9005c83f4e5) | ![Repaired candidate: both unknown tool rows visibly say No result; success remains unmarked](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e93c83ff-893c-4f41-87af-bfed8342787c) | Before is an inspected frame from the negative-control XCTest recording. After is the final passing run’s step-labels-expanded attachment. Only image metadata was stripped for publication; pixels were not changed. Raw xcresults/logs are retained with Colin’s Mac-agent evidence, not independently rerun or inspected by RoboClaw here. Two earlier negative-control attempts did not reach the intended assertion (AX startup timeout and fixture-readiness failure) and are **not** counted as regression proof. The report retains those failures separately; the definitive negative and final positive runs used separate exact-source builds on the same task simulator. Current exact-head [CI run 37692589347](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37692589347) and its openclaw/ci-gate passed, including native-i18n and the scoped lint check. The earlier broad [Testbox run 37666559471](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37666559471) passed build/typechecks but stopped on five inherited max-lines errors; that historical failure is not relabeled as a pass. Current CI skips some broader native jobs; the focused native proof above is the missing changed-surface acceptance. Source inventory verification and independent complete-candidate source review also passed. Physical-device, live Gateway, macOS rendered UI, iPad accessibility/RTL and broader presentation variants remain outside this focused acceptance. ### Original contributor proof — predates the repair The following logs and images describe the original proposal, not the repaired candidate. In particular, the old after-image did not retain a visible unknown-outcome cue on iPhone; the maintainer repair addresses that gap. Original commit on `a51a76bda63`. Authoritative proof `step-labels-proof6`, same final test on both trees: - **Before:** base plus fixture and UI test only. One test failed at line 785: `XCTAssertFalse failed - Step still uses the unknown-outcome fallback: exec - outcome unknown pr` (13.167 seconds). The prepared status assertion passed. - **After:** the same test passed (14.052 seconds); it also requires the row's accessibility value to retain “No result,” rather than infer success from the raw result. - Shared kit: **2,289 tests in 194 suites passed** (32.843 seconds); XCTest additionally ran 61 tests, 2 skipped, no failures. - SwiftFormat on source/kit files and strict scoped SwiftLint: clean. The UI-test file retains one existing long-line wrap finding (base line 571, branch line 572 because of the Vision import). - macOS app build passed; scratch tree restored clean. Full TypeScript build/check/test and CI have not been run for this Swift-only change. [Proof log](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/550e05da401987d0793392bc92daa50d11a093b2/ios-step-labels/proof.log) · [Independent review](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/550e05da401987d0793392bc92daa50d11a093b2/ios-step-labels/review.md) | Before, original base | After, original proposal (not repaired candidate) | |---|---| | | | Both historical screenshots are from the original proof above. Cropped identically at the bottom to omit the composer's synthetic fixture model label; the step and final reply are unchanged and remain visible. The screenshot UI regression uses a small synthetic fixture in the existing local-demo transport, with an ended Exec activity that has no status. It opens the completed-work disclosure, OCRs the rendered row, asserts “Exec” is present and “outcome unknown” is absent, and confirms the final reply is still present. It inspects pixels because the accessibility label already used the local tool title before this change. The `preparedTitle` test covers unknown terminal activity falling back to the local title while running and completed Gateway titles stay intact. The existing unknown-outcome test still requires “No result,” not “Finished,” even when a raw result is present. On a device build carrying this change plus unmerged changes, the step rows showed the tool's own title. **Not covered:** - A live Gateway round trip from the isolated PR build, or recovering missing terminal outcome facts. - macOS rendered UI (the shared source is built for macOS), iPad, VoiceOver, and alternate text sizes or appearances. - The device observation was on a build with additional unmerged changes, not this isolated PR build. An independent review caught the original accessibility-only test gap; it was replaced by the rendered-pixel assertion and re-reviewed. AI-assisted (Codex).
